c.v: Yes. There is a formal inventory reconciliation process in place that covers both Courier and Formal operations. Reconciliation is performed daily, exceeding the minimum requirement of at least twice a week. In Courier, the reconciliation report is prepared daily, saved in the corporate repository (SharePoint), and forwarded to the support analyst for consolidation and generation of management dashboards in Power BI, enabling continuous monitoring, traceability, and tracking of any discrepancies. In Formal, the reconciliation control includes verification upon shipment arrival, as provided for in the applicable operational procedures, as well as an additional control, which consists of extracting shipment status from the HMS system and comparing this information with the shipments physically stored in the secure area (cage) through physical scanning. The generated reports are properly archived in a specific folder in Teams, ensuring traceability, documentary evidence, and compliance with regulatory requirements for inventory reconciliation. If systemic issues are identified, a corrective action plan is in place to address the root cause and prevent recurrences.

c.v: Yes. DHL Express employees who perform customs-related activities in Brazil possess the necessary qualifications, in accordance with local customs regulations and DHL’s internal Operational Instructions, which define job profiles, responsibilities, and mandatory training. Brazilian customs legislation does not require DHL Express employees to hold an individual Customs Broker license with an expiration date. Customs broker credentials are regulated, controlled, and published by the Customs Authority itself (Brazilian Federal Revenue Service). If a customs broker loses their authorization, access to customs systems is automatically blocked, preventing them from performing their duties. Thus, active status confirms the validity of the authorization. DHL Express maintains documentary evidence of appointments and credentials, as well as internal controls aligned with the official mechanisms of the Customs Authority.

Yes. Customs clearance records for imports, exports, and transit are maintained in an organized, traceable, and accessible manner for a minimum period of 5 years, or as required by applicable regulations.
Formal Import: Documentation is stored digitally in the corporate system (iShare), with access controls. The original documents accompany the shipment for the customer’s safekeeping; when not picked up, they remain physically stored in controlled areas (airport or storage provider).
Formal Export: Archiving is fully digital, with documents available in official and corporate systems (Portal Único/RFB, Connected, GIA/Sherloc).
Informal: ANVISA and MAPA documents remain archived at MCT for an indefinite period exceeding 5 years, and RFB release records are stored on the Portal Único.
Spot checks are conducted as required, with documented evidence available in the retention systems.

c.v: For informal import operations, when permitted by Brazilian customs legislation, pre-arrival customs declarations are processed promptly and in accordance with regulatory requirements. The data is fully cleaned, validated, and entered into the local application (Connected), including all mandatory information for the customs declaration, such as Incoterms®, customs value, tariff classification, and country of origin. After validation, and within the regulatory deadline (up to 4 hours before the flight’s arrival in Brazil), a formal notification is sent to the GTW department to proceed with the operational steps. As evidence, the daily log of processed flights, with their respective details, is attached. For Formal Imports, it is clarified that Pre-Arrival Customs Declarations are neither provided for nor practiced in Brazil.

This is achieved through document verification by the clearance team and physical inspection using X-ray scanning. The Held return team also conducts an analysis based on the description of the contents in the packing list.
Formal: For IMP Formal shipments to be released at our warehouse, the identification of the goods and their classification as restricted/prohibited is performed prior to processing the shipment for our warehouse, through analysis of the Customs Clearance Instruction form, completed by the customer, which contains all product descriptions. Given this preliminary analysis, shipments of goods restricted/prohibited by our network do not enter our warehouse. Attached is an example of a Clearance Instruction for a case that was denied because it involved a restricted/prohibited product in IMP Formal (used product).

Formal Export: In the Formal Export process, consignments are subject to evaluation and cargo presence by the customs agency, after the procedures have been completed and the relevant documents issued. To ensure compliance and operational control, there is a systemic lock that prevents the physical movement of the shipment before all the mandatory steps have been completed. This lock is linked to the issuing of the physical label, which is necessary for the identification and movement of the cargo. The system only allows the label to be printed once the process has been completed, ensuring that no shipment is moved before it has been duly authorized.

c.v: Como parte del plan de mejora, el área definió las siguientes acciones para 2026 – Gestores Gateway (Art. 174): - Presentación de documentación : Es fundamental evitar la entrega de documentos que puedan generar observaciones o dudas durante la revisión por parte del funcionario DHL. - Cumplimiento estricto de requisitos : Se debe asegurar la entrega exacta de la documentación solicitada por Aduanas. No se debe aceptar documentación informal o declaraciones firmadas. Siempre se debe respaldar el proceso con documentos formales, tales como: Factura firmada por el proveedor,Cartolas bancarias, Documentos verificables y trazables - Escalamiento semanal de casos sin resolución : De manera semanal, se deben escalar a la jefatura de Aduana Courier todos los casos (DIPS) que se encuentren pendientes de resolución. - Revisión diaria de guías : Es obligatoria la revisión diaria de todas las guías, sin excepción, con el fin de evitar acumulaciones y retrasos en la operación.

c.v: During the examination, the information from the customs worksheet is used simultaneously to verify the manifest information, mostly for the intercepted awbs for physical examination. If at any time during the examination something is revised, it is noted on the manifest where it is amended also on customs worksheet for final handover for release of the cargo. IF there is an unsatisfactory agreement between shipment infomration and broker and customs, shipment is detained for further information to clarify unsatfied infomration.

c.v: Envio OUT: están controlados por DPA y requieren secuencia de ckpts especificas. Adicional a esto, los envios que no llevan tramite formal (hace el BROKER) son puestos a disposicion de la DNA quienes deciden que sale y que no. Los que no salen son puesto por estos en una jaula. Envíos IN: -DOX Son verificados y analizados por Aduanas quienes autorizan el release. -NON DOC 75% de envíos arribados quedan retenidos con intervencion obligatoria del broker. El 25% restante es fisicamente verificado por DNA previo a liberación, por lo que cualquier envio que se haya autorizado su liberacion es responsabilildad de la DNA. En caso de detectarse envíos mal liberados Aduanas solicita apoyo a DHL, de forma solidaria, para el reingreso de los mismos y subsanar el error. Se adjuntan los ultimos ejemplos

c.v: As explained by Alan M. Updated facility authorization is only required when a facility is moved or physically modified. The primary points of the approval that must be kept up-to-date are the employee list and bonded inventory. A new employee list must be submitted to CBP anytime there is a change. The previous list should be compared to current management roster. Inventory is not required to be submitted to CBP, Gateway employee reporting is expanded to include a quarterly report of all employees with access to the secure area. (19 CFR 122.184)
